overview:
Oregon's sixth district leans Democratic by about six points, and incumbent Andrea Salinas is seeking re-election with a commanding financial edge. She has raised roughly $1.6 million and holds about $611,000 on hand, while Republican David Russ has reported around $13,000 raised and just $21 in cash. Outside spending has been minimal and only in support of the incumbent.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win around 95%. The combination of incumbency, a favorable partisan lean, and a vastly better-funded campaign points to a comfortable Democratic hold, though the absence of polling leaves some uncertainty about the exact margin.
